neighbours.label: boundedness of extent: finite vs infinite / endless, across languages
fire: In calculus we often ask whether a series has a finite sum or not.
Euclid showed that there is an infinite supply of prime numbers.
The hallway of mirrors created an endless row of reflections.
Engineers modelled the beam with a mesh of finite elements.
The game world is effectively boundless, stretching on in every direction.
Für Kinder scheint der Sommer oft unendlich lang zu sein.
Он рассказывал бесконечные истории о своей молодости.
Our patience is not infinite, the manager warned the team.
quiet: In calculus we often ask whether a series has a positive sum or not.
Euclid showed that there is a simple proof about prime numbers.
The hallway of mirrors created a bright row of reflections.
Engineers modelled the beam with a mesh of small elements.
The game world is effectively huge, stretching on in every direction.
Für Kinder scheint der Sommer oft sehr lang zu sein.
Он рассказывал смешные истории о своей молодости.
Our patience is wearing thin, the manager warned the team.

predictions: Fires on finite, infinite, endless, boundless and their German/Russian equivalents (unendlich, бесконечный); quiet when the same slot holds a size word (large, long, huge).
notes: Card: infinite/finite x14, unendlich, бесконечные, 인피니티. Probes: finite 0.695/0.473, unendlich 0.786, бесконечные 0.467, endless 0.415, limitless 0.294; 'large amount' 0.006, 'indefinitely' 0.033. The meaning (bounded vs unbounded) carries it, not one word.
